claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct: steker denotes the connector fitted to the end of an electrical cable and inserted into a power outlet.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: steker

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct: palam denotes a two- or three-pin electrical device connected by wire and inserted into a socket; plag is also listed as a synonym.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian Malay answer: palam

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correctly specifies an electrical plug inserted into an electrical socket, distinguishing it from other senses of plug.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: different-common-word is accurate for the localized standard/common terms steker and palam, despite possible informal use of plug in both varieties.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: The cited dictionary entries establish meanings but do not quantify informal frequency of plug in either variety.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No material false friend is present. Palam also has a general stopper/seal sense, but the electrical sense is explicitly established and matches the cue; steker is not misleading for this sense.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both answers accurately denote an electrical plug in their respective varieties. Indonesian steker and Malaysian Malay palam are established terms; the English cue and sense are aligned. The relation different-common-word is appropriate. No material false-friend contrast is present, though informal plug may occur in both varieties.
